life: Hardy herbaceous perennial from fleshy roots, 1–2 ft, clumping
edible_parts: Young leaves, tender stems and flowers.
other_uses: Pollen-rich flowers worked heavily by bumblebees in the morning; the flowers close by afternoon. A classic cottage-garden native.
prep: Young leaves and stems eaten raw in salads or cooked briefly like a mild green; they are mucilaginous, which thickens soups. Flowers make an edible garnish.
harvest: Leaves and stems spring through early summer, before flowering toughens them; flowers May–July.
risks: Sap can irritate sensitive skin. Do not confuse young growth with that of daylily or iris in mixed plantings — iris is toxic.
buy: Widely offered by native nurseries; many named cultivars exist, so ask for the straight species.
